title: Front Turn vs Reverse Turn Box-Out
description: A technique drill that teaches both box-out turns: the front turn to meet a crasher head-on and the reverse pivot to seal a player who is close.

content.objective: Learn when to use a front turn and when to use a reverse pivot to box out, and perform both with balance.
content.setup: Pairs: one attacker, one defender, a step apart in front of the basket.
content.organization: Coach calls 'front' or 'reverse' each rep; swap roles every four reps.
instructions: Defender in stance facing the attacker, one arm's length apart.
Coach calls 'front': step toward the attacker, make chest contact, then turn to face the rim.
Coach calls 'reverse': pivot on the foot nearest the attacker's path, swing the back into them.
Hold the seal with a wide base and arms up for two seconds.
The attacker tries to get round at walking pace, then full speed.
coachingPoints: Front turn when the attacker is far, reverse when close.
Contact first, then look for the ball.
Wide base, low hips, arms up.
commonMistakes: Turning before contact and getting pushed under.
content.safety: Contact is with the body and forearms only: no pushing in the back, no undercutting a jumping player.
progressions: Attacker starts from a random spot.
variations: Use only reverse turns on post players.
Do it from the help line.
content.gameApplication: The right turn at the right distance keeps attackers from walking in for put-backs.
